Vengeance game: Ermine, Proletariat, Fright Train and Friction head to Silver Gulch and find Chrono-Ranger, Sky-Scraper, Tempest and Omnitron-X.

Proletariat gets both his problem cards out early, but there's plenty of area effect damage and ongoing destruction on the hero's side so you can manage it. Also the environment is fairly helpful.

Mint, but everyone on around 7 hp. Hit hard, hit often and you'll be fine.

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Near Mint.

 

First game, I made two critical errors:

1. I used Micro Assembler on Omnitron X, forgetting that you need to discard a card as a part of its power. I had Defensive Blast in my hand and a plating out, so my intent was to fish for another plating, thinking "WOW, once I get this set up, the game will be a cakewalk! I'll show them how a robot rampages!" and then, since Defensive Blast was the *only* card in my hand at that point, I had to discard it, and Omniton X hung his head and cried cyber-tears of shame and sorrow.

 

2. I left Ermine for last. Why?  Uh...dunno. Lapse of Judgment? Flight of Fancy? Not paying attention? I thought--"Eh, I can ride it out."  Nope. Bad idea. Sky-Scraper went down at some point, but I had CR, Tempest and O-X in mid-single digits with only Ermine left. She soon produced 2 Subtle Diversions simultaneously, and I had no way to get rid of them. I watched all the HP slowly go away while I frantically tried to draw some ongoing destruction (which this team has plenty of...I had just squandered it early and wasn't drawing any more).

 

So Ermine stood victorious with about 5HP left.  

 

Second game went MUCH better. I took out Ermine relatively early, and had almost no problems. Sheriff Pratt ended the game by shooting Proletariat while boosted with 2 Aggression Modulators. That lawman was MAD!

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Powerhound_2000:

My guess is because overall her threat isn't taking out the heroes by damage but moreso screwing up any setup.  

With the exception of Iron Legacy, it seems to me that screwing up set-up is what makes a villain difficult, not ability to do damage.

I mean, look at the higher rated villains – Citizen Dawn's "avoid at all costs" card is Devastating Aurora, which does no damage. Gloomweaver was downgraded from a 3 to a 1, and I'm pretty sure the fact he has no forced ongoing/equipment destruction has a lot to do with that. While Voss is still rated at 3, I tend to find him consistently easy, because his deck has one card that does any Ongoing destruction, and it's a unique target with no in-built way to come back.

And of the lower-tier villains, the worst cards to face are the Flechettes and Devious Disruption because they wipe your board.

By this point in the game, there are tons of healing or DR options for most of the heroes, making damage itself less of a threat, while the real danger is losing the cards and combos you've spent the whole game setting up.

Easy Mint with 11/8/8/13 HP remaining. All four enemies went down in my third round.

Tempest was far and away the MVP. Gene-Bound Shackles is total shenanigans in Vengeance as it is against the Ennead. By the time it came around to his third turn, Fright Train was down and everyone else was at 4 or less, making them easy pickings.

Hopefully I don't have to redo it - I see the latest iOS update is screwy - but I won't mess with anything until it gets fixed, and hopefully my one-shot collection is unaffected.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
Mint, although it was a largely un-fun slog.   HP 7/7/7/6.  

 

Despite trying to kill Ermine first, Ermine and Freight Train (Choke, plus the "wipe out one person's hand unless everybody discards a card") left me with few options from the get-go.   It's weird -- I hadn't played many Vengeance games, so I played a large number of practice games (7+) before this one.  In *every single game,* I managed to get Skycraper in Huge form by her 2nd round, and was able to lay waste effectively.  In this game, she never had a single Huge card in hand until the very last turn, when she used Rest and Recover to pull it out of the trash.  She was stuck in Tiny form the whole game and couldn't come out, and never even had enough cards in her hand to use her Tiny power effectively; I think she played 3 links the entire game.  

 

Likewise for Omni.  His hand was also pretty devastated, and despite playing Reset and using his power on himself every turn to try to pull out extra cards, he never got the Ablative Coating he needed, or any of the "play/draw extra cards" Components.  Two Disruptive Flechettes proved moderately useful.

 

Chrono plinked away every turn, but only ever had one bounty in play, and didn't get his Hat until mid-/late-game.  Even then, like Sky-scraper, he never really had enough cards in his hand to do anything super-useful.  He did manage to play his one bounty ("By All Means") on Ermine, and between that and Hunter and Hunted, it helped to take her down fast.

 

Tempest was the biggest damage dealer, via Grievous Hail Storm and the Gene-Bound Shackles. 

 

Cyrus Hayes and the Sheriff were a big help in taking out the Nemeses, the Clones, and Friction's equipment.

 

Either way, not much fun on this challenge.  No cool combos, no multi-card plays, no characters playing off each other...no real strategy at all.  Just a battle of attrition:  "Heroes take their turn, do some damage," then "villains take their turn, do some damage."  The heroes had a few more HP to start, and did a little more damage every round, so they won, but not through any clever or inventive play on my part.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
OK, here it is.
 
Round 1:
 
Ermine: Chrono-Ranger discards Danny-Boy, Sky-Scraper discards Undetectable Relinking, Tempest discards Into the Stratosphere (because O-X is blowing up the Ongoings anyway), and O-X discards Reactive Plating Subroutine.
 
Chrono-Ranger plays Terrible Tech-Strike, dealing 2 to Ermine and 1+1 to Fright Train.  Uses base power on Friction.
 
Proletariat does his thing.
 
Sky-Scraper plays Neutralizing Resonator on Fright Train, then uses her base power.
 
Fright Train does his thing.
 
Tempest plays Gene-Bound Shackles and uses his base power.  Order / decisions matter a little; you can shoot yourself out of 1 damage to a Proletariat clone if you choose poorly.  Basically, hit one clone (say "no"), hit the other clone, then hit Proletariat and say "no" again.
 
Friction does her thing.
 
Omnitron-X uses Sedative Flechettes and destroys Constant Prattle and Defensive Formation.  Again, the damage order matters a little with Proletariat and clones.  Hit the 5 HP clone, then Proletariat himself, then it doesn't matter anymore.  Use base power on Tempest, put Grievous Hailstorm into play.
 
Silver Gulch plays Sustain the Portal.  Do not discard, everything takes 2.  Kill the Proletariat clones first.
 
Round 2:
 
Ermine does her thing.
 
Chrono Ranger plays Just Doin' My Job, which discards Ranger's Mark, Micro-Assembler, Shielding Winds, and Defensive Blast.  CR pings Fright Train with JDMJ's damage, then uses base power on Fright Train.
 
Proletariat does his painful thing.
 
Sky-Scraper destroys Everyman's Strength with Neutralizing Resonator, plays Tectonic Chokeslam on the Shock Dampeners, and uses base power.
 
Fright Train does his thing.
 
Tempest plays Chain Lightning. Friction for 6, Fright Train for 6, Ermine for 4.  Then, Grievous Hailstorm on Proletariat, Ermine, Friction, Crackjaw Crew, and Fright Train, in that order, to hit them all for 4.
 
Friction does her thing.
 
Omnitron-X plays reset and pulls Singularity. Plays Singularity, blows up Gene Bound Shackles.  Use base power on Chrono-Ranger, Sudden Contract pulls By Any Means and puts it on Proletariat, pings Proletariat.
 
Silver Gulch plays Sustain the Portal again.
 
Round 3:
 
Ermine does her thing.  I put Hailstorm back.
 
Chrono Ranger plays Eye on the Prize and pings Ermine, then draws The Whole Gang, playing it on Fright Train.  Base power on FT, TWG destroys Proletariat. 
 
Proletariat does his incap thing.
 
Sky-Scraper uses Tectonic Chokeslam and uses her base power to end the game.
